subject: Demo + value-check: proposed trial & acceptance sprint for Montage Analytics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@montageanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Demo + value-check: proposed trial & acceptance sprint for Montage Analytics

Hi Anna / Tom — thanks again for your time today. Appreciate you walking us through the ingestion challenges and the downstream lag that’s blocking analyst productivity. Quick recap and a suggested path to trial so we can validate the three value signals you called out (faster retrieval, reduced annotation load, and cost per inference).

Recap (from our call):
- Scope: pilot on the ‘Customer Support Tickets’ corpus (last 18 months).
- Success signals:
  1) 40% reduction in average latency for the retrieval+generate flow (target p95 < 600ms)
  2) 20% drop in manual tagging time on triage tasks (measured by annotation throughput)
  3) Normalize inference cost to < $0.015 per 1k tokens via batching/quantization config
- Constraints: data residency in us-east, no PHI in the pilot, read-only access for our connector, and a two-week measurement window.

Proposed trial outline (high level):
1) Prep (3 business days): dataset snapshot, access for a scoped service account, and confirm metric hooks.
2) Run (10 business days): Redwood-hosted trial cluster with a single model family (opt-13b-quant), two traffic patterns (batched vs low-latency), and daily evaluation.
3) Acceptance sprint (3 business days): joint review, drive-by QA, and formal acceptance sign-off against the three success signals.

Owners / next steps:
- Montage: provide sample dataset and a contact for secure access (Tom?) — estimated due 2028-06-21.
- Redwood: we’ll provision trial infra and a short eval harness (Marissa).
- Measurement: Ben will share a simple scoring sheet and dashboard links.

Attachments: attached a draft MAP (Mutual Action Plan) and our recommended Redwood POC configuration file. I also uploaded the demo recording to Drive (link below).

Please let me know if you want to narrow the scope (fewer intents) or extend the measurement window. If this looks good we’ll provision the trial Monday and aim to have the first runs by Wednesday.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com
(415) 555-0183

Attachment stubs: Montage_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 85KB), redwood-poc-config.yaml (text, 3KB), demo-recording-20280618.mp4 (mp4, 42MB)

From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@montageanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo + value-check: proposed trial & acceptance sprint for Montage Analytics

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and close to what we discussed. A few clarifications:

- Tom will be primary for data access (I looped him below). He can provide an S3 snapshot and temporary IAM role.
- We prefer the measurement window to be 14 calendar days to capture weekend spikes.
- For success signal #2, we’ll use our internal annotation tool’s throughput metric (average items/hour per annotator). Can Redwood ingest those logs or do we need to export?

Two small asks:
1) Can you add an explicit rollback plan if the model runs into hallucination cases during the run?
2) Can you point us to the exact metric names you’ll populate in the MAP so our analytics team can pre-map fields?

Assuming those items are answered, we’re good to confirm. Thanks —
Anna
Head of Data Science | Montage Analytics
anna.lopez@montageanalytics.com

Hi all — I can provide a read-only IAM role and an S3 snapshot. I’ll schedule a 30-minute handoff with our infra team Tuesday morning to transfer credentials.

Regarding annotations: we can export annotator throughput as a CSV by day, and we’ll include a small sample of raw annotation logs. Is that format OK for Redwood?

Ben / Marissa — I’m aiming to have the data and role in place by 2028-06-21 EOD. Also, Anna asked about a rollback: our preference would be a simple toggle to revert to live inference (our current vendor) if we see >5% incorrect label rate on a sanity sample during the run. Happy to adopt Redwood’s recommended guardrails — please propose one.

Thanks,
Tom

Subject: Re: Demo + value-check: proposed trial & acceptance sprint for Montage Analytics

Hi Tom / Anna — thanks for the quick replies and for lining up the S3 access. A few notes from Redwood side and concrete responses to your asks: 

1) Metric ingestion: the CSV export of annotator throughput is perfect. We’ll share a small ingestion script (Python) that your infra team can run to drop the preprocessed file into the trial bucket; Stephanie will own that artifact.

2) Rollback / guardrails: proposed safety plan (summary):
  - Canary: run 5% of traffic through the new model for 24 hours after the first provisioning.
  - Sanity checks: daily random sample of 200 items scored and compared to ground truth; alert if >5% label mismatch.
  - Auto-failover: if an alert triggers, traffic is cut over to baseline (current vendor) and we open a joint investigation ticket.

3) Measurement window: we can extend to 14 calendar days (no issue). We’ll mark the MAP with both business-day and calendar-day variants so you have explicit expectations.

Immediate next steps (timeline):
- 2028-06-21: Montage provides S3 snapshot + IAM role and sample annotator CSV.
- 2028-06-22: Redwood provisions trial cluster and sends access to monitoring dashboards.
- 2028-06-23 to 2028-07-06: Measurement window (14 calendar days).
- 2028-07-07 to 2028-07-09: Acceptance sprint and sign-off.

Deliverables we’ll send today: updated MAP (v1.1) with metric field names, ingestion script, and a short runbook for the canary/failover.

I’ll also propose two short calendar invites: a Tuesday handoff for credentials (Tom + infra) and a Thursday kickoff for the trial run verification (stakeholders only).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
